caption: The drawing features a single horse standing in profile facing to the right. The horse has a dappled gray coat with dark spots distributed over its body, and its legs are lighter in color, appearing almost beige or off-white. The mane, drawn with fine lines, is dark, likely black or dark brown, and flows down the crest of the neck. The tail is similarly dark and bushy, extending outwards and slightly to the left. The horse's head is slightly bowed, and it has a naturalistic yet stylized appearance with simplified anatomical details. The background of the drawing is completely plain and off-white, with no additional objects or scenery. There is text in the bottom right corner, reading “Prime Saddle.”
title: Horse
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
